subject: Acadia Health — evaluation & regression hardening proposal
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: alice.morgan@acadiahealth.com; procurement@acadiahealth.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Evaluation & regression hardening proposal for Acadia RFP

Hi Alice / Acadia procurement team,

Thanks for sharing the RFP. Attached is a concise evaluation and regression regimen that maps to NIST AI RMF outcomes and EU AI Act deployment controls (summary + appendix). High-level approach:

- Baseline evaluation: model-card verification, prompt-anchored test suites, and safety checks (toxicity, hallucination, PII leakage).
- Regression cadence: nightly unit-level checks, weekly sampling regressions on production-like traffic, and gated pre-release runs for rollouts.
- Traceability: per-request artifacts, deterministic seeds for evals, and summary diffs for model updates.
- Governance: playbook for severity triage, automated rollback triggers, and manual human-in-the-loop review for high-impact regressions.

Deliverables included: evaluation-regimen PDF (attached), sampling templates, and a README for integrating our test harness with your CI.

Key asks from Acadia to proceed:
1) Confirm desired sensitivity thresholds for safety signals (e.g., allowable hallucination rate per 1k responses).
2) Approval to run a 2-week shadow evaluation on a synthetic/obfuscated sample of your production prompts.

I’ve CC’d Marissa from Product for any technical clarifications and program-level SLAs.

Next steps: If this aligns, we’ll schedule a 30-min technical walk-through and propose a pilot timeline.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Jonas —

Thanks for the rapid turnaround and the detailed deck. A couple of clarifying questions from our side before we can greenlight the shadow evaluation:

- On "allowable hallucination rate": can you provide an example acceptance threshold set you normally propose for clinical triage scenarios? We need a starting point we can share with clinicians.
- For the shadow evaluation, will Redwood require any PHI? We prefer obfuscated/synthetic data and would need a short MOU for data handling.
- Regarding rollback triggers: how do those integrate with our incident response — e.g., will Redwood trigger automatic throttling or do you provide alerts and wait for our approval?

Cc'ing Dr. Santiago for clinical acceptability and Legal for data handling/MOU. Also looping in Procurement to confirm potential pilot costs.

Appreciate it,
Alice Morgan
Senior Manager, Procurement
Acadia Health

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com; ben.carter@redwood.com; grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 08:47:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Acadia clarifications — need quick edits and positions

Folks — forwarding Acadia’s clarifying questions. Need concise responses we can send back (and a redline of the regimen doc). Proposed replies below — please edit inline: 

1) Hallucination threshold: propose 5/10k for triage scenarios as a starting point; escalate >20/10k to "high-impact" triage. (Marissa: is 0.05% baseline conservative enough?)

2) Data for shadow evaluation: we will accept obfuscated/synthetic datasets. We should propose a 2-paragraph MOU draft that says Redwood will only process synthetic data, will not persist raw utterances beyond retained artifacts, and will provide ephemeral logs for analysis. (Ben: can you draft?)

3) Rollback triggers: recommend automated throttle + alert pipeline: Redwood can auto-throttle new sessions and pause model rollout on severe infractions, but any account-level full rollback will be coordinated with Acadia and/or named contacts. (Grace: confirm ops behavior and SLA windows.)

I’m attaching the regimen PDF with trackable comments for quick redline. Need a consolidated reply by end of day Wednesday so I can send to Acadia Thursday.

Thanks,
Jonas

Attachments included: 20261120-redwood-eval-regimen-v1.pdf

Jonas / team —

Quick edits and suggested wording (high level):

- Hallucination threshold: propose 5/10k as "operational baseline" and 15/10k as "actionable" for clinical triage; include a footnote that thresholds can be tuned per clinical pathway. Reason: clinicians tolerate a slightly higher recall/precision tradeoff for recall-first triage but want clear escalation.

- MOU/data handling: Ben has drafted a two-paragraph MOU (see filename below) that states: no PHI ingestion, must be synthetic/obfuscated, logs retained for 14 days encrypted at rest, and we will delete ephemeral artifacts after analysis. Also propose a short addendum offering an on-site (or VPC) pilot if they require additional isolation.

- Rollback behavior: Grace confirms we can do automated throttles on specific endpoints and can pause rollouts immediately. Full account-level rollbacks require a 1-hour response SLAT for enterprise-tier customers; include this in the reply as a commitment.

I created a redlined PDF and exported a clean copy. Attaching both here.

Marissa Cole
VP, Product
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Evaluation & regression hardening proposal for Acadia RFP — updated materials and pilot steps

Hi Alice / Acadia team —

Thanks for the questions. Per our internal review (cc'd Marissa, Ben, Grace), please find our updated position and next steps below. We’ve attached the redlined regimen as well as a concise MOU for the shadow evaluation.

Responses to your items:

- Hallucination threshold: We recommend an operational baseline of 5 incidents per 10k responses for clinical triage and classify >15 incidents per 10k as actionable/high-impact requiring escalation. We’ll include per-pathway tuning during pilot and provide clinical sampling reports for your review.

- Synthetic data and MOU: We will only accept synthetic/obfuscated prompt sets for the shadow evaluation. Please review the attached two-paragraph MOU (mou-acadia-shadow-draft.txt). We will not ingest PHI; logs will be retained encrypted for 14 days and then purged unless you request extended retention.

- Rollback and incident handling: Redwood can apply targeted throttles and pause model rollouts automatically upon detection of high-severity signals. Full account rollbacks will be coordinated; for enterprise customers we commit to a 1-hour SLAT to acknowledge and begin rollback coordination. We will emit alert packets (detailed event records) to your incident channel and provide a human point-of-contact during the pilot window.

Pilot proposal (2-week shadow run):
1) Kickoff & data handoff: Week 0 — MOU signed, Acadia provides obfuscated/synthetic prompt set (max 10k prompts).
2) Baseline evaluation: Week 1 — run tests, produce initial sampling report.
3) Regression tuning & report: Week 2 — run production-like sampling, deliver final report and recommended guardrails.

Attachments: 20261126-redwood-eval-regimen-v1-redline.pdf, mou-acadia-shadow-draft.txt, 20261127-acadia-response-pkg.zip (contains runbook + sampling templates + CI integration snippet).

Links: https://redwood.app/drive/ACD-2026-037/eval-regimen-v1 (read-only), HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.com/deal/ACD-2026-037

If the above looks good, we can schedule a 30-min technical walkthrough next week (I have openings Tue/Wed mornings PST).

Best regards,
Jonas Weber
